label: VERIFIED
extraction: Adversarial Review (AR) introduces a minimal cooperative code-review protocol with three agents: main coding agent, reviewer, and critic. The reviewer evaluates code while the critic audits the review through structured disagreement before the main agent edits. AR outperforms a five-agent baseline on LiveCodeBench using only three agents. On SWE-PRBench, naive AR exposes a false-consensus failure mode where agents converge on agreement without sufficient evidence, but a single prompt iteration adding explicit disagreement constraints achieves highest F1. Two execution modes tested: Python orchestrator for controlled comparisons, and portable SKILL.md protocol for autonomous agents like Claude Code. Key insight: cooperative code review requires minimal, structured, evidence-grounded disagreement — not more agents. Maps to ECC santa-method dual-reviewer pattern and council adversarial review.
